physical_base.name: Fixed wiring base
physical_base.replacement: not a 5-minute module: every field plug is unscrewed and moved plug by plug; no individual wire moves

expansion_terminal_contract.adopted: Section 03 D03-4: M8-M11 and ENC4-ENC11 terminate on the XTB expansion terminal board, fitted once and then part of the fixed wiring; MX4 and EX8 stay replaceable behind it
expansion_terminal_contract.cost: XTB with 136 headers and plugs: estimate $104-167 per expanded unit; carrying the headers on every base instead adds about $35-43 per 8-motor unit
expansion_terminal_contract.usability: twelve-motor units ship with the XTB fitted, so their wiring never changes; a field upgrade fits the XTB once (two studs and one guided connector, no soldering), then the card
expansion_terminal_contract.alternative: all 136 expansion terminals on the base: one wiring diagram for every unit and no XTB part, paid by every 8-motor unit

permission_placement.decision: Adopted from section 04 section 6.2: WD_M, WD_O, both arm latches, the OPI_TX, OPI_BOE and OPI_OUT latches, the PERMIT_OUT_REQ gate, the DIC_OK filter and the final permission gates on the motion card; tamper latches on the PSM, which owns logic power-on reset; an OUT_EN latch on every output card.
module_reasons: the user's decision puts the FPGA 'with its clock, configuration flash and supervisory circuitry' on the replaceable motion card
every latch input originates on the MC; only permission outputs and EXT_PERMIT, PROCESS_PERMIT, RAILS_OK and TAMPER_N cross a connector, so a connector fault can only remove permission
watchdogs and FPGA are factory-tested and replaced together; the self-test of section 04 section 5.4 runs after every MC replacement
the fixed base stays passive (section 03 D03-1), so no permission silicon can force a base replacement
each receiving card has its own pull-down and its own local AND with presence and power-good

rejected.fixed base: active silicon on the base; a base replacement cannot meet the 5-minute target
rejected.PSM: separates the watchdogs from their WDI sources by two connectors; the PSM keeps only the tamper latches because it owns POR

permission_placement.reconciliation: Section 04 section 6.3 routes MX4 'through the base Ioff buffer'. IS-1 places that Ioff buffer on the motion card (this section governs card boundaries); equations and filters are unchanged.

host_link.physical: one SPI bus, mode 0, MSB first, active-low chip selects, FPGA oversampled at 50 MHz core; SCLK <= core/8 = 6.25 MHz; budget cases 5.00 and 6.25 MHz

CS_FB.response_magic: CNF3 (or a page: CAP3, FLT3, IDP3, card MAINT response)

rules: exact length per chip select (1408 or 768 rising SCLK edges); shorter, longer, early release or both chip selects asserted together: rejected, LINK fault
snapshot at synchronized CS assertion; commit only after CS release with exact length, CRC and semantic validation
CS guards >= 8 core ticks before the first rising edge and after the last falling edge, >= 8 ticks high between transactions
big-endian fields; u24 counters are low 24 bits of 32-bit FPGA counters, unwrapped by the host modulo 2^24
one sequence counter shared by both chip selects: next = last + 1, nonzero, no wrap; FB_READ, READ_PAGE, MAINT and NOP use sequence 0 and do not advance it
ABI byte 0x03 in every frame; no fallback to ABI 1 or 2 (CNC1_BAD_CAPS)
per_cycle_order: cnc1.read: CS_FB FB_READ (event ack) -> CNF3 feedback
LinuxCNC motion, kinematics and HAL functions
cnc1.write: CS_CMD UPDATE (rates + outputs) -> CNS3 (event, telemetry, timing)

frozen_IS1.iol1_hardware_gates: output enable = qualified OUT_PERMIT_k (hardwired, section 04) AND OUT_EN latch Q AND CARD_EN (MCU pin with pull-down). The OUT_EN latch (one half of an SN74LVC2G74DCUR on each DO and ACC card) has D = 1, CLK = MCU OUT_EN_ARM strobe, asynchronous CLR_N = the qualified OUT_PERMIT_k net, so any accepted OUT_PERMIT_k drop, however short, turns the outputs off and keeps them off; the MCU reads Q, reports the drop (realtime b6 of the status byte), writes SW_STATE = 0 and re-arms the latch only in ACTIVE after a new epoch and IO_ENABLE. The ACC uses the second half the same way for PROC_PERMIT (PEN latch)
